title: Add capability-gated operational actions after v1
notes: apps/membrane-hub/src/actions.mjs, apps/membrane-hub/tests/actions.mjs, docs/hub/actions.md, operations/hub/actions/hub-actions.v1.json, and tests/hub-actions/actions.test.mjs already existed on this tree from an earlier, incomplete pass at this same task (commit d3b72347, message 'feat(hub): add capability-gated action request contract'). That pass defined the six post-v1 actions (restart, reconcile, rotate-token, review-proposal, restore-quarantine, apply-update), each with a distinct hub.action.* capability and a repair/hub/<action> repair path, plus buildHubActionRequest: a pure builder that turns a snapshot + draft into either an inert, frozen 'awaiting-trusted-runtime' request or a fail-closed 'unavailable' result (unknown action, missing/malformed confirmation nonce, missing capability grant, or invalid payload). It never dispatched, never claimed success, and never produced a receipt itself -- that authority was left entirely to a future trusted runtime.

That prior pass left a real gap: the JSON schema (operations/hub/actions/hub-actions.v1.json) already documented an immutable runtimeReceipt shape, but nothing in the JS layer ever validated a receipt against it or proved a receipt was actually bound to the request that produced it. A future trusted-runtime backend could in principle hand the Hub a well-formed-looking but forged, replayed, or wrong-action receipt and the UI would have had no way to detect it. This task closes that gap.

apps/membrane-hub/src/actions.mjs: buildHubActionRequest now also computes and freezes a requestDigest -- a sha256 (node:crypto, stdlib, no new dependency) over the canonical (key-sorted) actionId, capability, capabilityReceiptId, confirmationNonce, and payload. A new export, applyRuntimeReceipt(request, receipt), is the only path from a pending request to a rendered outcome: it rejects any receipt that is not shape-valid against the existing JSON-schema contract (closed outcome enum, ISO timestamp, repair/hub/<action> pattern, bounded identifiers), and it independently rejects any receipt that is shape-valid but not cryptographically bound to the exact request (mismatched actionId, capabilityReceiptId, requestDigest, or repairPath) -- both cases render 'unavailable', never an optimistic success. A bound receipt whose outcome is 'rejected' renders 'rejected', never 'proven'; only a bound, shape-valid receipt with outcome applied/repaired/rolled-back renders 'proven'. Every outcome (unavailable, rejected, proven) surfaces the action's repairPath so a failed or rejected action always has a visible repair route. A new renderer, renderHubActionStatus(request, outcome, root), is a read-only DOM projection: it only ever sets root.innerHTML and HTML-escapes every evidence field, matching the same read-only/escapes-evidence contract already enforced elsewhere in the Hub (apps/membrane-hub/src/agents-adapters.mjs, test 'renderer is read-only and escapes evidence').

apps/membrane-hub/tests/actions.mjs and tests/hub-actions/actions.test.mjs gained new deterministic node:test coverage proving: every action's capability and repair path are distinct; every built request carries a stable, nonce-bound requestDigest; a shape-valid, correctly bound receipt is the only way to reach 'proven'; a runtime-rejected outcome never becomes 'proven'; a receipt with a tampered digest, wrong repair path, or invalid outcome enum is rejected as 'unavailable'/'receipt-not-bound-to-request' or 'receipt-shape-invalid'; a receipt can never be applied to a request whose capability grant was never present in the first place ('no-pending-request'); and the renderer escapes hostile actionId content, never mutates any root property besides innerHTML, and never renders a proven success for a rejected outcome. All prior tests (capability/nonce/payload gating, builder never dispatches) still pass unmodified.

operations/hub/actions/hub-actions.v1.json gained a new optional top-level 'request' schema formalizing the exact live request-instance shape (state const 'awaiting-trusted-runtime', kind const 'hub.action.request', bounded actionId/capability/capabilityReceiptId/confirmationNonce/rollbackOrRepair, and the new requestDigest sha256 pattern) alongside the pre-existing 'actions' and 'runtimeReceipt' schemas. It is additive only: 'request' is not added to the root 'required' array, so any prior consumer that only validated 'actions'/'runtimeReceipt' remains valid.

docs/hub/actions.md was extended to document requestDigest, the receipt-binding contract enforced by applyRuntimeReceipt (shape validation, cryptographic binding, rejected-never-proven, repair path always surfaced), and the read-only renderer contract.

engine/crates/membrane-runtime/**, apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/** (other than the explicitly excluded files), and operations/hub/actions/** dispatch wiring were deliberately NOT touched. The landed Rust Hub facade (engine/crates/membrane-runtime/src/hub.rs) hard-codes HubCapabilitiesV1.read_only = true and HUB_OPERATIONS = ["hub.capabilities", "hub.snapshot"] only -- no action-dispatch operation exists there, and this task's own instructions require preserving that invariant ('the Hub renderer is deliberately READ-ONLY today ... preserve that property'). Wiring a real trusted-runtime dispatcher into the Tauri backend would flip that invariant and is out of scope for a Wave 4 task whose acceptance is explicit capability + confirmation + immutable receipt + repair path at the request/proof-of-receipt layer, not live execution. This task therefore delivers the full client-side request/proof contract a future dispatcher must satisfy, without granting the Hub any new ability to execute or claim success on its own.

No cargo build/test/check/clippy/fmt, no Tauri or pnpm release build, and no mutating git command was run. The manifest commands (cargo fmt --check, cargo test --workspace, pnpm --dir apps/membrane-hub test, cargo check --manifest-path apps/membrane-hub/src-tauri/Cargo.toml) were not executed as a batch; per MEMBRANE-BOOK-MODE-EXECUTION-RULES.md they run once at the final phased book gate (Gate phase 3.2 -- Wave 4 phase). Only the task's own new/updated test files were executed directly with node --test, plus the full apps/membrane-hub/tests/*.mjs suite to confirm no regression -- see commands.log.
